items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: I'm not saying that everyone have to be a drama school graduate, but that element of entertainment, since television has come in, entertainment is at a high level now. So I think we are in competition with the rest of the world, not James Alley or nothing like that.

ctx.x: Almost finished. Are there any specific things you'd like to see done in New Orleans to encourage artists, either commercially or to have more confidence in themselves? Yes.

Sharpen up the acts. I do believe that, in spite of what New York has as downfall, and people talk about it, there are drama schools, there are good music schools, there are other good colleges. There's quite a bit of learning you can do on the street there, too. But there's so many good schools, and there are plays that you can go and see. There's the Winter Garden. There's the whole Broadway element. That if a kid is serious about what he's doing, he can think that I can maybe be right down there on Broadway…
Do you listen to any of the jazz groups in town?
